facts.statement: The genus Presbyornis was first described by Wetmore in 1926.
The genus includes the type species P. pervetus, as well as P. recurvirostra, P. isoni, and the disputed P. mongoliensis.
facts.quote: subdivision: * P. pervetus Wetmore, 1926 (type) P. recurvirostra (Hardy, 1959) P. isoni Olson, 1994 "P." mongoliensis Kurochkin & Dyke, 2010

facts.statement: Presbyornis was previously known by the synonyms Nautilornis and Coltonia.
This extinct bird lived in North America during the Late Paleocene and Early Eocene epochs of the Paleogene period.
facts.quote: Presbyornis is an extinct genus of presbyornithid bird from North America during the Paleogene period, between the Late Paleocene and Early Eocene.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence from the Early Eocene Green River Formation suggests Presbyornis nested in colonies and may have died in mass events like volcanism or botulism.
facts.quote: The fossil record of P. pervetus includes many complete skeletons from Green River Formation sites (Early Eocene), suggesting that the birds nested in colonies and that they possibly died due to volcanism or botulism

facts.statement: The species P. recurvirostra is known from a partial wing found in the Late Paleocene to Early Eocene Colton Formation near Ephraim, Utah.
facts.quote: P. recurvirostra is known from a partial wing (KUVP 10105) found in the Colton Formation, from the Late Paleocene to Early Eocene sediments of the Wasatch Plateau near Ephraim, Utah.

facts.statement: The species P. isoni is known from the Late Paleocene Aquia Formation in Maryland and is much larger than P. pervetus.
facts.quote: P. isoni, much larger than P. pervetus, is known from the Late Paleocene Aquia Formation in Maryland

facts.statement: Specimens attributed to P. mongoliensis from the Early Eocene of Mongolia are fragmentary and likely belong to a stem Phoenicopterimorphae rather than the genus Presbyornis.
facts.quote: The holotype and paratypes of "P." mongoliensis are known from the Early Eocene of Mongolia, but these fragmentary specimens are poorly preserved and they likely belong to a stem Phoenicopterimorphae, not a presbyornithid.

facts.statement: Presbyornis could stand up to 1 meter tall due to its long legs and neck.
facts.quote: Because of its long legs and neck, Presbyornis could stand up to 1 m tall

facts.statement: Presbyornis had a broad, flat bill used for filtering small plants and animals from water, similar to modern dabbling ducks.
facts.quote: Its broad, flat bill was used to filter food (small plants and animals) from the water, in the manner of today's dabbling ducks.

facts.statement: The fossil range of Presbyornis spans from the Late Paleocene to the Early Eocene.
Presbyornis belongs to the family Presbyornithidae.
P. pervetus was duck-sized with longer legs, while P. isoni was larger, exceeding the size of a swan.
facts.quote: P. pervetus tenía un tamaño similar al de una oca, pero con las patas más largas mientras que P. isoni, conocido a partir de unos pocos huesos, era más grande, superando el tamaño del cisne.

facts.statement: Complete skeletons of P. pervetus from the Early Eocene Green River Formation suggest the bird nested in colonies and was vulnerable to botulism.
facts.quote: El registro fósil de P. pervetus incluye muchos esqueletos completos de la Formación Green River (Eoceno inferior), lo que sugiere que esta ave hacía sus nidos en colonias, y era especialmente vulnerable al botulismo, como muchos otros anseriformes de la actualidad.

facts.statement: P. recurvirostris is a disputed species that may be a synonym of P. pervetus.
facts.quote: P. recurvirostris es una especie discutida que podría ser sinónima de P. pervetus

facts.statement: Presbyornis lived between 60.9 and 33.9 million years ago, from the Selandian to the Priabonian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Selandian to Priabonian (60.9 to 33.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Presbyornis is now classified as a member of an extinct group of anseriforms most closely related to modern screamers.
rejected.quote: it is now considered a member of an extinct group of anseriforms which was most closely related to modern screamers.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'a member of an extinct group of anseriforms'
